title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
A man used AI image generation technology to create sexually explicit images of a college acquaintance without her consent, then distributed them across multiple social media platforms under fake identities. He obtained source photos from her private social media accounts and used several email addresses and fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook to conceal his identity while spreading the content. This is a case of impersonation and harassment enabled by AI that generates synthetic sexual imagery, deployed by a user with malicious intent toward a specific person.

The victim learned of the harassment through anonymous messages alerting her to the manipulated images on Discord servers. She reported it to police, who traced the fake accounts and email addresses to identify the perpetrator. The investigation recovered digital evidence from his mobile phone and SIM cards. What is not established is whether the AI system used had safeguards against this type of misuse, or whether it was deployed in a way that made such impersonation and non-consensual sexual imagery possible to create.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading sexually explicit AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a recent engineering graduate, obtained photos from the woman's private social media accounts and used artificial intelligence technology to create obscene morphed images. He then distributed the content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using several email addresses to hide his identity.

The victim discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her manipulated photos and videos were being shared on Discord servers. She filed a complaint with the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi, prompting an investigation that analyzed digital evidence and social media trails. Police traced the fake accounts and email addresses back to Bansal, who admitted during questioning that personal resentment from college had motivated his actions. Investigators recovered his mobile phone and SIM cards as evidence, and the investigation continues.
